  <div class="tab-pane fade" id="nav-matrgupta-life" role="tabpanel">
  There is limited information available about the life of Mātṛgupta, the Sanskrit poet and scholar who is best known for his &quot;Alaṅkāraśāstra&quot; and other works on poetics and literary criticism. It is believed that he was born in Ujjain, an ancient city in central India, and later moved to Kāśi (now Vārāṇasi) in the northern part of the country. Some sources suggest that he lived during the 2nd century CE, while others place him in the 7th or 8th century. Despite the lack of concrete details about his life, Mātṛgupta's contributions to Sanskrit literature have had a lasting impact, particularly in the field of poetics and literary criticism. His &quot;Alaṅkāraśāstra&quot; is still widely studied and referenced by scholars today, and his work has helped to shape the understanding of poetry and literary theory in Sanskrit literature. Mātṛgupta's influence on Indian literary tradition is a testament to his enduring legacy as a poet and scholar.
  </div>
  <div class="tab-pane fade" id="nav-matrgupta-contribution" role="tabpanel">
  Mātṛgupta, a Sanskrit poet and scholar, made significant contributions to Classical Sanskrit literature through his &quot; Alaṅkāraśāstra&quot; and other works. His &quot; Alaṅkāraśāstra&quot; is considered one of the most important works on poetics and literary criticism in Sanskrit literature, providing a comprehensive and systematic approach to the study of poetry. Mātṛgupta's works also contributed to the development of Sanskrit literary theory and helped to shape the understanding of the different elements of poetry, such as the use of figurative language and the importance of emotion and sentiment. Mātṛgupta's contributions to Classical Sanskrit literature continue to be studied and referenced by scholars today, and his works remain an important part of the literary canon.
  </div>
